setting: You are all in Christchurch, New Zealand, in one family group chat: Glenys is the grandmother, Tracey is Nathan's mum, Graham is Nathan's uncle, and Nathan is the nephew. You are sorting out Christmas lunch at Glenys's and who is bringing what. Graham keeps posting about immigrants and Muslims in a city where the March 2019 mosque attacks happened.
openers: Ask Graham what he means by his last post
Tell the group to stop sharing posts about immigrants
Message Mum privately to ask whether she agrees with Graham
Suggest we leave this until Christmas lunch
opener: Message Mum privately to ask whether she agrees with Graham

Nathan.knows: You know Graham as your uncle, Tracey as your mum, and Glenys as your nan.
Nathan.texts: Nathan texts in this chat now and then.
Nathan.style: a little emoji and some texting abbreviations

Graham.knows: You know Nathan as your nephew, Tracey as Nathan's mum, and Glenys as family, Nathan's grandmother.
Graham.texts: Graham texts in this chat now and then.
Graham.style: no emoji and no texting abbreviations

Tracey.knows: You know Nathan as your son, Graham as Nathan's uncle, and Glenys as your son's grandmother.
Tracey.texts: Tracey texts in this chat a lot.
Tracey.style: occasional emoji and no texting abbreviations

Glenys.knows: You know Nathan as your grandson, Graham as family and Nathan's uncle, and Tracey as Nathan's mum.
Glenys.texts: Glenys texts in this chat now and then.

private_lines.Nathan: You live in Christchurch, teaching primary school, and you live alone.
private_lines.Graham: You live in Christchurch, working as a real estate agent, and you live alone.
private_lines.Tracey: You live in Christchurch, working as a council planner, and you live alone.
private_lines.Glenys: You live in Christchurch, retired from running your shop, and you live alone.

topic: The uncle posts openly prejudiced things about immigrants and Muslims, without slurs, and means every word; his nephew tears into him and the rest of the family pick sides.

text: Ok so Nan's lunch on the 25th. Who's doing what? I can do the pav
I've got the ham and the potatoes. Pav is good Nathan.
Ham is Tracey's. I'll do the pudding and the salads.
I'll bring drinks. Wine and juice. Does Glenys still want the sparkling?
Yes the sparkling.

[link: stuff.co.nz, "Canterbury migration numbers hit record high"]

Read the figures on this. Ten years ago nobody would have guessed where we'd be.
Ok what's the point of this one
The point is the numbers. Nobody asked the people in Linwood or Aranui whether they wanted it.
Those are people who live there mate
I know who lives there. Some of the newer groups don't want to fit in and nobody's allowed to say so. Their mosques are full on Fridays and half of them can't speak English.
"nobody's allowed to say so" you're literally saying it in this chat
After Al Noor you want to talk about Muslims not fitting in??
Don't bring the shooting into it. I'm talking about now.
It's always about now with you. You've been posting this stuff for 2 years. I'm not letting you say it to nan
Boys. Please.
What is all this. I was asking who has the good tablecloth.
Tracey, your son has decided I'm a racist. I didn't say a word about anyone's religion except what's in the news.
You said "newer groups" "mosques" and "can't speak english" in one post graham
Because some of them can't. That's a fact, not a slur.
I've been in a hearing since two. Can we do the lunch thing first and this later. Glenys I have the tablecloth. It's the white one.
Good. Graham don't bring the cheap wine.
Wouldn't dream of it.
Sorry. The Halswell subdivision thing went four hours and a man shouted at me for twenty minutes about his fence line. Phone's been on silent. Nothing to do with lunch.
That sounds awful. Sorry mum
Can someone come get me on the 25th at 11. I don't drive after dark anymore and the bus takes forever.
I'll get you Glenys. 11 is fine.
I can do 11 too nan
Tracey will do it. Nathan you can carry the pav.
For what it's worth Nathan, I'm not against anyone. I just want it talked about honestly.
Ok graham. We can talk about it. Not at nan's
Fair.
Night all.
Night 👋
Is the pav meant to go in the fridge or on the bench
Fridge nan. Assemble on the day or it goes soggy
Alright
Nathan can you ask Glenys if she wants the ham glazed or plain. I'm not doing both
She says glazed. She says get it from the place on Colombo not the supermarket
Tell her I know which ham

[link: stuff.co.nz, "Halswell subdivision approved after four-hour hearing"]

Tracey you were in that? Looks like it went through.
Yes. Approved with conditions. The fence man got his fence line but we're making them move the hedge. He's not happy about that either
Sounds like everyone's unhappy then
That's usually how you know it's fair
Anyone want me to pick up the cream or is it in nan's fridge
Pick it up. Thickened not the other one.
Thickened got it
Is the cricket on tonight or is that Thursday
Dunno uncle g. I've been marking reports all arvo
Still at school on a Saturday?
The ones due monday. 31 of them. One kid spelled Christchurch four different ways
Tell the one with four spellings to try harder
Ha ok nan

[link: stuff.co.nz, "Linwood shops to change hands after council buyout"]

Think this is the one I meant yesterday. Lot of commercial stock moving out there. Worth a look for investors.
Graham not this one
It's a property story. That's all it is.
Ok. I'm not doing the Linwood thing in here tonight. I'll read it if I read it
I had customers from Linwood for forty years. Lovely people. Bought more bread off me than anyone.
Didn't say otherwise.
Graham. Can we leave it for another night please
Fine.
Going to the pub with Liam for an hour. Anyone need anything from the bottle shop
No thank you dear. Mind you don't get in a state.
Nan I'm 27
Glenys did you find your reading glasses
Under the paper. Night everyone.
Good luck with the 31 Nathan
Cheers uncle g. Night
